subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: May OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical exec review inputs within one reviewer/run, and what exact fields must be part of that cache key?
rationale: The defect is real, but caching a model-backed approval reviewer result changes when later exec requests bypass a fresh review, so this needs approval-boundary intent rather than an automatic repair.

options.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
options.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the complete ExecAutoReviewInput or generated prompt, without persisting or converting the result to durable approval.

options.title: Memoize allow-once only
options.body: Cache only low-risk allow-once results and keep ask, timeout, and error outcomes uncached for a narrower behavior change.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Accept the repeated model cost to preserve one fresh reviewer completion per approval miss until stronger security or billing evidence changes the tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
recommendation.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the complete ExecAutoReviewInput or generated prompt, without persisting or converting the result to durable approval.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest routing candidate from the normalized auto mode PR ownership and current approval-boundary context.
